profile.headline: Software Engineer at IBM
profile.summary: I’m a software engineer with a few years of experience working in middle-ware for IBM’s WebSphere Application Server. Currently, I’m the Lead Developer for their Web Services team, where help to design, plan, implement, and support WebSphere’s Web Service features. I contribute heavily to WebSphere's open source project Open-Liberty. Prior to that, I contributed to the Liberty profile’s managed deployment of non-Liberty micro-services like Docker and API Connect, as well as, developing Liberty’s javaMail-1.5 feature.

positions.title: Jr. Software Engineer
positions.description:
I provide excellent Web Service Level 3 technical support for WebSphere customers that require an engineer to have direct access to product code for our JAX-RPC, JAX-WS, JAX-RS features. I resolve problems by analyzing logs and source code, recreating scenarios it in a test environment, and providing fixes to the product when required. 

Occasionally, I serve as defect monitor, where I proactively monitor the Web Service team’s automated test infrastructure. When failures occur, I open and triage defects, then I assign them to the proper owner or resolve them myself. I work with Release Management to ensure that all defects are resolved before release’s ship. 

I contributed to an expansion of Liberty’s collective server management technology, which allows a Liberty based collective controller to deploy and manage non-Liberty micro-services like API Connect and Docker. 

I adapted older code provided with traditional WebSphere to the newer Liberty profile, where I open sourced and stored the changes for public consumption on GitHub. 

I developed the javaMail-1.5 OSGi feature for WebSphere’s Liberty profile. 

I have delivered Unit, BVT, a FVT tests for product code that either I or a team-mate has written. 

I volunteer as Developer Buddy, where I help new hires and prospective IBMers learn more what it's like to work in IBM, and help in anyway I can as a feel Software Engineer as they integrate into their new position.

positions.title: Student Worker
positions.description:
As a student worker, I provided systems support for the Vice President of Student Affairs

- I maintained computer hardware, printers, and software for Vice President of Student Affairs Department.   

- I provided technical support for end-users on Windows OS, and 3rd party software. 

- I configured and deployed workstations including hardware and software. I backed up end-user data, and restored machines using Symantec GhostCast software.   

- Trained new-hire student workers on technical practices and procedures

- I tracked projects, current work orders, and inventory on proprietary ticketing system.

positions.title: Sprint Customer Service Supervisor
positions.description:
At Teleperformance USA,  I managed a team of up 50 new-hire customer service representatives

- I trained and assisted in their development for the first two weeks of calls after they completing their class-room training.

- I consistently exceeded all client specified goals. 

- I had daily one-on-one coaching with each representative under my supervision. 

- I maintained top customer service records within the call center.

- I contributed new training programs for the entire call center staff on new products and procedures
